blocks.content: Letting $ i = 1 $, i.e., using the elements in the first row of A, $$ \left|\mathbf{A}\right|=1\cdot(-1)^{1+1}\left|\begin{array}{l l}3&2\\ 2&1\end{array}\right|+1\cdot(-1)^{1+2}\left|\begin{array}{l l}1&2\\ 1&1\end{array}\right|+1\cdot(-1)^{1+3}\left|\begin{array}{l l}1&3\\ 1&2\end{array}\right| $$

Using Equation 8.12a to obtain the determinants of the $ 2 \times 2 $ matrices, this simplifies to $$ \left|\mathbf{A}\right|=\left[1\times(3-4)\right]-\left[1\times(1-2)\right]+\left[1\times(2-3)\right]=-1 $$

The same answer is obtained regardless of which row is used, and expanding around a column, instead of a row, produces the same result. Thus, in order to reduce the number of computations required to obtain a determinant, it is useful to expand using the row or column that contains the most zeros.
